record_type_quote: The current study examined the generalizability of the moral foundations hypothesis (Graham, Haidt, & Nosek, 2009), which predicts that conservatism will be positively related to the binding foundations (i.e., virtues of ingroup/loyalty, authority/respect, and purity/sanctity).

targets.authors: Graham, J., Haidt, J., & Nosek, B. A.
targets.title: Liberals and conservatives rely on different sets of moral foundations.
targets.evidence_quote: The current study examined the generalizability of the moral foundations hypothesis (Graham, Haidt, & Nosek, 2009), which predicts that conservatism will be positively related to the binding foundations (i.e., virtues of ingroup/loyalty, authority/respect, and purity/sanctity).
targets.outcome_quote: Thus, our findings provide one clear example in which the moral foundations hypothesis does not replicate well, but future research can explore competing explanations for why the hypothesis was weaker in Black people.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Overall verdict says the moral foundations hypothesis does not replicate well, consistent with the title. Weaker positive relationships alone do not override that verdict.

reasoning: Two new samples retest the published conservatism-binding-foundations relationship explicitly attributed to Graham, Haidt, and Nosek (2009). Study 2 repeats this paper’s Study 1 and is aggregated, not counted as an original. Graham et al. (2011) supplies the MFQ and methodological context; other theory and related evidence citations are not independent targets of the named hypothesis test.
